headline: QA-focused roundup: agentic QA tools, LLM evaluation benchmarks, mobile-device security APIs, and programmatic quality gates that change how teams test and enforce release quality.

top_signal.title: Android Bench 2.0 adds long‑horizon tasks and agentic evaluation
top_signal.summary: Google upgraded Android Bench to 2.0 with long‑horizon tasks, continuous scoring, and agent-level evaluations to measure LLMs and agents on multi‑day, multi‑step Android engineering work. The leaderboard and methodology were updated.
top_signal.why_it_matters: Provides a rigorous, reproducible framework QA teams can use to evaluate LLMs and agents for real developer workflows and to design acceptance criteria for agentic test automation.

items.title: Junie Local: JetBrains ships a fully on‑device coding agent
items.summary: JetBrains released Junie Local (on‑device Junie) that runs a tuned Qwen3.6‑27B model on M5 Macs (64GB RAM). It runs the same agent loop locally, removing network/tokens and enabling private, unlimited agent runs.
items.why_it_matters: Local agents let QA run many iterations privately, reduce cost of repeated test-generation tasks, and enable offline, NDA‑safe experimentation with agentic test flows.

items.title: Junie /demo: a reproducible demo VM for agentic UI testing and video evidence
items.summary: Junie’s /demo mode provides a reproducible demo VM template (demo‑base image + tooling) that agents can use to launch apps, drive UI, capture screenshots, video, and HTML reports for review.
items.why_it_matters: Makes agentic UI runs auditable and repeatable — useful for automated exploratory flows, regression video evidence, and machine‑reviewable test artifacts in QA pipelines.

items.title: GitHub adds REST API to manage 'Restrict code coverage' ruleset
items.summary: GitHub now exposes a REST API to create, read, and update the 'Restrict code coverage' repository ruleset option, enabling programmatic enforcement of minimum coverage or maximum PR coverage drop.
items.why_it_matters: QA leads can now enforce coverage gates across many repos via infrastructure-as-code, automating coverage thresholds and integrating coverage policy into release pipelines.

items.title: AndroidX Security State libraries provide component‑level device patch posture
items.summary: AndroidX Security State (v1.1.0) and Security State Provider (v1.0.0) expose component‑level patch and update status so apps can programmatically query OS/module/kernel patch posture instead of a single SPL value.
items.why_it_matters: Mobile QA can now gate features, simulate patch states, and validate enterprise flows against real component‑level device security posture for more accurate device compatibility testing.

items.title: NVIDIA publishes AIPerf for realistic, high‑concurrency LLM inference benchmarking
items.summary: NVIDIA introduced AIPerf (replacing GenAI‑Perf), a multiprocess LLM benchmarking tool that avoids client bottlenecks, supports 15+ endpoint types, and uses public datasets and trace replays for realistic workloads.
items.why_it_matters: QA and SRE teams evaluating LLM‑backed test agents can use AIPerf to measure latency, throughput, concurrency, and detect client-side bottlenecks under realistic traces.
